sections.h2: What kind of place is Denver for property tax purposes?
sections.html:
Denver is a consolidated city and county, so one government handles what a city and a county handle elsewhere. According to Wikipedia, it consolidated as the City and County of Denver on December 1, 1902, and it is described as the only U.S. state capital that is a consolidated city-county.

Adams, Arapahoe and Jefferson counties surround it. The city covers about 154.7 square miles, sits at an official elevation of 5,280 feet, and was platted on November 17, 1858 at the meeting of Cherry Creek and the South Platte River. The 2020 census counted 715,522 residents, and the page gives a 2025 estimate of 740,613.

For a seller, the consolidation means one set of offices. The Assessor values your house, the Treasury Division bills the tax, and the Clerk and Recorder files your deed, all inside the same city government.

sections.h2: Which Denver neighborhoods and employers shape the housing market?
sections.html:
Denver has 78 official neighborhoods, and the Wikipedia article lists the City and County of Denver, Denver Public Schools, the State of Colorado, Denver Health and United Airlines as top 2023 employers.

Government, energy and mining, telecommunications and logistics are the sectors the article names.

sections.h2: What does Denver weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Hail is the main weather risk the sources point to. Wikipedia says Denver ranks tenth among U.S. cities of 50,000 or more for hailstorm exposure and has had three of the ten costliest hailstorms in the country.

The climate is cool and semi-arid with about 3,100 hours of sunshine a year and roughly 49 to 53 inches of snow. For owners, that points to roof age and condition as a recurring question. Roof age and condition are worth knowing before you talk to any buyer.

sections.h2: How is Denver property tax figured?
sections.html:
Taxes equal actual value minus a value reduction, times an assessment rate, times the mill levy. The Denver Assessor FAQ gives the 2024 figures in the table.

Property typeValue reduction per parcelAssessment rate
Residential$55,0006.7%
Commercial improved$30,00027.9%
All other$027.9%

Denver's combined general mill levy for 2024 was 79.202 mills, or 0.079202. Taxing authorities set levies in December, and levies and rates change from year to year, so treat these as 2024 numbers and look at your own bill.

Real property is reappraised every two years, in odd-numbered years. Residential values come from the market approach, using sales in the 24 months ending June 30 of the prior year.

sections.h2: When is Denver property tax due?
sections.html:
Half is due on the last day of February and half on June 15, or the whole amount by April 30. The Treasury's property tax calendar lays out the year.

  • January: annual tax statements are mailed.
  • April 1: deferral applications are due.
  • April 30: full payment due, and the elderly and disabled refund application deadline.
  • May through August: delinquency notices are mailed.
  • July 1: later delinquencies become available for tax lien buyers to endorse.
  • September and October: delinquent taxes are advertised in the local newspaper.
  • October: the real estate tax lien auction is held.

Denver also lists July 15 as the application date for senior and disabled veteran exemptions, and an April 15 date for personal property declarations. The calendar does not list penalty or interest rates, so ask Treasury for the payoff on any delinquent account.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Denver property value?
sections.html:
The protest deadline is June 8 each year, or the next business day if June 8 falls on a weekend or holiday. You can file in writing, in person or online with the instructions on your Notice of Valuation.

Include your reasons, evidence such as sales of similar homes or condition problems, your parcel or schedule number and a daytime phone number. If you disagree with the decision, you can go to the State Board of Assessment Appeals, to District Court, or to binding arbitration.

The Assessor also says you may protest up to two prior years' values that you did not protest at the time, using a Board of County Commissioners petition for abatement or refund of taxes.

sections.h2: Can seniors or active military defer Denver property tax?
sections.html:
Colorado runs a deferral program through the county treasurer, and applications run January 1 to April 1. The state treasury says it covers owners 65 or older and active-duty military who meet its rules.

For seniors, the page requires age 65 by December 31 of the year, residence at the property, prior taxes paid, liens and mortgages of no more than 75 percent of actual value, and no reverse mortgage. The deferral is a loan recorded as a junior lien, with interest running from May 1. A sale or contract of sale makes repayment due 90 days later.

Anyone selling a Denver house with a deferral on it should ask for the payoff early, so the title company can include it at closing. Active-duty military applicants have a different test: liens, mortgages and deferrals together must stay under 100 percent of actual value for VA-guaranteed loans, or 90 percent otherwise.

sections.h2: What happens if you sell a Denver house with property tax due?
sections.html:
The title company asks Treasury for the amount owed and pays it from your proceeds at closing. You do not have to find the money first.

The sooner the account is current, the fewer steps remain. An account that moved toward the October lien sale needs the lien buyer's payoff in addition to the tax. In that case, a title officer who knows Denver's process saves time.

If you owe back tax on a Denver house, are behind on payments or inherited it, we can send you a written cash offer for the house as it stands. You decide whether it works.

sections.h2: How do you get to and around Denver?
sections.html:
Denver International Airport is about 20 miles from downtown and serves as the city's official weather station. Wikipedia also notes that a commuter railway system began operating in the metro area in 2015.

The metro area has about 3.1 million residents, and its 2023 gross domestic product was $311.9 billion, the 18th largest among U.S. metro economies. Denver Public Schools alone employed about 12,700 people in 2023.

sections.h2: What are Denver service liens for storm drain and sewer?
sections.html:
Denver mails separate lien statements for storm drain and sanitary sewer service, and these can show up on a property alongside regular tax. The Treasury calendar says storm drain statements go out in February, April, June and August, and sanitary sewer statements in March, May, July and September.

If a seller has an unpaid service lien, the title company will find it in its search and list it as a payoff. Ask Treasury about the balance early.

For general city questions, Denver lists 3-1-1, or (720) 913-1311 from outside the city, as its main number.

faqs.q: When is Denver property tax due?
faqs.a: The first half is due the last day of February, the second half June 15, and full payment April 30. Dates falling on a weekend or holiday move to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the Denver property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: June 8 each year, or the next business day. You can file in writing, in person or online per the Notice of Valuation.

faqs.q: What was Denver's mill levy in 2024?
faqs.a: The Assessor's FAQ gives a combined general mill levy of 79.202 mills for 2024. Levies are set each December, so use the figure on your current bill.

faqs.q: How often does Denver reappraise homes?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years. Residential values use only the market approach, based on sales in the 24 months ending June 30 of the prior year.

faqs.q: Does Denver run a tax lien sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent taxes are advertised in September and October, and the real estate tax lien auction is held in October, per the Treasury calendar.

faqs.q: Does selling a Denver house trigger the property tax deferral repayment?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale or contract of sale makes repayment due 90 days afterward under Colorado's deferral program.
